goal: zig-waf takes out the share of its CRS request time that is its own, before zig-regex gets faster: patterns compiled the way ModSecurity compiles them, and capture work only on the rules that match.
scope: Test `@rx` with a span-only compile, and run the capturing compile only when a rule matches and needs its captures
Keep every `@rx` on zig-regex's linear engine where its semantics allow, instead of the backtracker
Cut per-request bytes on the CRS path: zig-waf allocates 1.1 MiB per clean GET and 3.8 MiB per 973-byte form, against ModSecurity's 0.9 and 1.8 MiB
Record `zig build lab` numbers before and after each change in docs/benchmark-lab.md
out_of_scope: Reaching ModSecurity's latency, which needs P2.21 (P9.39)
Byte-mode and dotall compilation of `@rx` (zig-utils/zig-waf#89 and #90), which this builds on
Moving @pm and phrase matching onto zig-regex literals (P9.09)
notes: Profile in zig-utils/zig-waf#86 at 374f61a: 82% of crs-form-post's time is inside zig-regex's backtracker and under 3% in transformations. Moving every pattern onto the linear engine saved about 18% on CRS's 294 patterns, with the same verdicts
Four rules take 38% of the form's time (934100, 942360, 942190, 941140), and the top 25 take 74%
The lab's first results (zig-utils/zig-waf#6, f6a40a2): zig-waf is the cheapest engine with no rules and loads CRS fastest, so the gap is in rule evaluation
accept: `zig build lab` p50 drops on crs-get, crs-form-post and crs-json-post against 374f61a, on the same machine, with the numbers in docs/benchmark-lab.md
Zero mismatches across every lab scenario, and the FTW and differential suites still pass

goal: The three-engine benchmark lab runs in CI, so every change to zig-waf's request path is checked against ModSecurity and Coraza for decisions and recorded for speed.
scope: A CI job that builds ModSecurity 3.0.16 and Coraza 3.7.0 at the commits CI already pins, checks out CRS 4.28.0, and runs `zig build lab -Doptimize=ReleaseFast`
Cache the libmodsecurity build so the job does not rebuild it on every run
Fail the job on any engine error or decision mismatch
Upload results.md and results.json as an artifact
out_of_scope: Failing CI on latency regressions: shared runners are too noisy for a timing gate
notes: The lab needs Zig 0.17.0-dev.1857 or newer because zig-bench, its memory sampler, requires it
Left out of zig-utils/zig-waf#6 because GitHub Actions did not start runs for recent pushes to zig-utils repositories, so a new job could not be tried
accept: The lab job runs on pushes to main and passes with zero mismatches
A run's results.md and results.json are downloadable from the job
A deliberately wrong expected decision in a scenario fails the job

goal: zig-regex matches OWASP CRS 4.28.0's `@rx` patterns at least as fast as PCRE2 without JIT, so zig-waf can run CRS as fast as ModSecurity.
scope: A benchmark of every CRS 4.28.0 `@rx` pattern against the zig-waf lab's inputs (its form fields, GET values, headers and five attacks), compiled the way zig-waf compiles them, next to PCRE2 10.47 with and without JIT
Profile the costliest patterns on the linear engine: CRS's large generated keyword alternations (PHP function names, Unix commands) and `(?i)` alternations with lazy quantifiers
Speed up those shapes in the lazy DFA, or with a literal prefilter in front of it, with identical match results
Record before and after numbers with the benchmark
out_of_scope: A JIT that emits machine code
Match and depth limits, and ruleset caches (zig-utils/zig-regex#16)
CRS patterns zig-regex cannot compile yet (zig-utils/zig-waf#89)
notes: Measured in zig-utils/zig-waf#86 on 294 patterns and 23 inputs: zig-regex 0.5.1 takes 41.1 ms as zig-waf compiles today and 33.6 ms span-only in byte mode, against 7.8 ms for PCRE2 without JIT and 0.9 ms with JIT. zig-regex 0.2.1 took 822 ms
benchmarks/pcre2 already has a PCRE2 harness to build the comparison on
CRS is Apache-2.0: vendored patterns carry its license and notice, or the benchmark reads them from a CRS checkout
accept: The CRS benchmark runs with one documented command
zig-regex's total time on it is at or below PCRE2 10.47 without JIT on the same machine
Match results equal PCRE2's for every pattern both engines compile, on every input
`zig build test` and the differential suites pass

goal: zig-waf runs CRS at or below ModSecurity 3.0.16's per-request latency in the benchmark lab, once zig-regex is fast enough to make that possible.
scope: Move zig-waf onto the zig-regex release that carries P2.21
Rerun `zig build lab` and fix whatever is left on the zig-waf side
out_of_scope: Changing any rule decision: the lab's zero-mismatch rule holds throughout
notes: Split from P9.37 because the gap is mostly zig-regex's matching speed (zig-utils/zig-waf#86)
accept: `zig build lab` shows zig-waf's p50 at or below ModSecurity's on crs-get, crs-form-post and crs-json-post, on the same machine and run
Zero mismatches across every lab scenario, and the FTW and differential suites still pass
